question: Chords AB and CD of a circle meet at point P (outside the circle), when produced. If AB = 9 cm, PB = (1)/(3) AB and CD = 5 cm, then the length of PD (in cm ) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the secant intersection theorem, PA × PB = PC × PD.

Given PB = 1/3 × AB = 1/3 × 9 = 3 cm, so PA = 9 + 3 = 12 cm.

Let PD = x cm, meaning PC = x + 5 cm.

12 × 3 = (x + 5) × x ⇒ x² + 5x − 36 = 0

On factorising, (x + 9)(x − 4) = 0 ⇒ x = 4 cm (ignoring negative value).

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of chord AB = 9 cm

Length of chord CD = 5 cm

PB = 1/3 × AB = 1/3 × 9 = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

When two secants of a circle intersect at an exterior point, the product of the entire secant segment and its external part is equal for both secants.

⇒ PA × PB = PC × PD
